name: Device Restart/Shutdown
summary: Adversaries may forcibly restart or shutdown a device in an ICS environment to disrupt and potentially negatively impact physical processes. Methods of device restart and shutdown exist in some devices as built-in, standard functionalities. These functionalities can be executed using interactive device web interfaces, CLIs, and network protocol commands. Unexpected restart or shutdown of control system devices may prevent expected response…

analytics.name: Analytic 1933
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol restart/reset command directed at a field device from a source not in the approved engineering workstation list, particularly where multiple devices receive restart commands within a short window. Documented precedent: Industroyer exploited CVE-2015-5374 via a crafted 18-byte User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet to port 50000 on Siemens SIPROTEC relays. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context;…

analytics.name: Analytic 2260
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies Industrial Control System (ICS) vendor engineering software initiating a device restart command from a Windows host outside a scheduled maintenance window. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.
